saw_lines: Parents compare high chairs, buggies and timing for weeks, then buy once per child and rarely come back.
So the sale is won in the first line, where a parent decides whether your question is theirs.
Your 30 live ads carry no proof number, so collect one, like a review count or orders shipped, and lead every new ad with it.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 17 Nov 2026
points: None of your 30 live ads shows a proof number, so a parent comparing high chairs has no reason to trust the deal. Collect one real number, like a review count or orders shipped, and lead every new ad with it.
0 of 19 copy ads carry an offer, so a first time buyer has no reason to act today instead of later. Put one first order offer or a Hauck chair bundle in line one of three new ads.

13 different openings run across 19 copy ads, and the biggest leads only 3. Nothing repeats enough to build recall. Pick the two best stories, the Hauck chair and the buggy timing question, and build the next batch only from them.

16 ads have run 60+ days, so some of your stories already hold their place in the feed. Build three more variations of the oldest winner, the Hauck chair story running across three ads, and run them beside it.
